conventions.convention: Surface intersection is evaluation of PD(γ) cup PD(δ) on the specified fundamental class, with cohomology-first cap and first-factor-first geometric intersection; reversing orientation negates it.
The ordered symplectic basis is a₁,b₁,…,a_g,b_g, with intersection blocks [[0,1],[-1,0]].

Holomorphic differentials are integrated along continuous paths using finite sums of local-primitive increments; singleton intervals have integral zero. Piecewise-C¹ paths recover contour integration.
Normalized differentials satisfy P(a_i,ω_j)=δ_ij and Π_ij=P(b_i,ω_j). The period lattice is Z^g+ΠZ^g; in genus zero it is {0} in the zero space and the Jacobian is a point.
Changing base point from p₀ to q₀ subtracts (deg D)u_p₀(q₀) from the divisor class. Degree-zero classes are independent; nonzero degree can also cancel a torsion shift.
Period, Jacobian and divisor results retain full AC where their suppliers require it; the Bergman and Szegő constructions assume countable choice only.
Bergman spaces use restricted Euclidean Lebesgue measure on the trace Lebesgue sigma-algebra, unique holomorphic representatives of L² classes, and the first-variable-linear pairing ∫f conjugate(g).
Arbitrary-index orthonormal expansions are finite-subset nets, conditional on a complete orthonormal system being supplied; its existence is not asserted.
The Szegő boundary space is the L² closure of continuous holomorphic traces on a bounded connected C¹ domain, for σ=c dS with c>0. Kernel construction additionally requires Szegő regularity.

Disc and ball Szegő formulas use normalized boundary probability measure. The distinguished-torus polydisc kernel uses product normalized Haar measure, separately from the nonsmooth topological boundary.
The Bergman metric is the Hermitian form with entries ∂z_j ∂conjugate(z_k) log K(z,z), without an extra scalar factor; its one-based indices alias the library's zero-based coordinates.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a compact connected genus-g Riemann surface, the a-period map is an isomorphism, the normalized matrix Π is symmetric with positive-definite imaginary part, and the period homomorphism is injective with full lattice Z^g+ΠZ^g. In genus zero the spaces are zero and the quotient is a point.

Assume full AC. For every integral homology class γ, every continuous singular cycle c representing γ, and every holomorphic differential ω, P(γ,ω)=∫cω. Integration vanishes on boundaries and agrees with the complexified de Rham comparison.

Assume AC. On a compact connected Riemann surface of genus g≥1, for closed smooth complex one-forms α,β, ∫Xα∧β=Σ_i(Πα(a_i)Πβ(b_i)−Πα(b_i)Πβ(a_i)). The descended de Rham pairing is nondegenerate; holomorphic differentials are isotropic.

Assume AC. For a degree-zero divisor D and a finite chain c of continuous curves with boundary D, there exists a weak solution f with local form z^D(p) times a smooth unit and, for every closed smooth complex one-form ω, (1/(2πi))∫X(df/f)∧ω=∫cω. For holomorphic ω the smooth form dbar(f)/f gives the same integral.
Assume AC. On a compact connected Riemann surface, a smooth (0,1)-form θ equals dbar(g) for a smooth g if and only if ∫Xθ∧ω=0 for every holomorphic differential ω.
Assume AC. For a degree-zero divisor D on a compact connected Riemann surface, D is principal if and only if u(D)=0 in Jac(X).

Assume AC. The Abel–Jacobi homomorphism Div⁰(X)→Jac(X) of a compact connected Riemann surface is surjective. The map X^g→Jac(X), (x_j)↦Σ_j(u(x_j)−u(a_j)), is also surjective and descends surjectively to the symmetric product.

Assume countable choice. For open Ω⊆C^m and nonempty compact K⊆Ω, sup-norm and first-complex-derivative bounds on K are finite constants times the L²(Ω) norm. An L² limit of holomorphic L² functions has a holomorphic representative, with uniform convergence of those functions and derivatives on K.
Assume countable choice. For a biholomorphism F:Ω→Ω′ of domains in C^m, J_F never vanishes and K_Ω(z,w)=J_F(z)K_Ω′(F(z),F(w))conjugate(J_F(w)). The weighted pullback g↦(g∘F)J_F is unitary.

Assume countable choice. On bounded domains the Bergman metric is positive definite. Its quadratic form equals K(z,z)⁻¹ times the attained positive supremum of |∂Xf(z)|² over the L² unit ball with f(z)=0, for X≠0. Biholomorphisms pull back the metric form.

Assume countable choice. With Lebesgue volume, K_D=1/[π(1−z conjugate(w))²], K_D^m=π^−m∏_j(1−z_j conjugate(w_j))^−2, and K_B^m=m!/[π^m(1−⟨z,w⟩)^(m+1)]. With normalized boundary probabilities, S_D=(1−z conjugate(w))^−1 and S_B^m=(1−⟨z,w⟩)^−m.
Assume countable choice. The ball and polydisc determinant/kernel quotients are respectively (m+1)^mπ^m/m! and 2^mπ^m; these constants are distinct for every m≥2.

Assume AC. The explicitly defined smooth projective model of y²=x⁵−1 is a compact connected genus-two curve analytically identified with the translation double-pentagon. For T(x,y)=(ζx,y) and the oriented real-y sheet C, C,TC,T²C,T³C form an integral homology basis, with five-orbit sum zero. Its normalized period lattice is {(p(ζ),p(ζ²)):p∈Z[t]}.

seams_checked.note: Opened the supplier page and the divisor, divisor-bundle, projective-chart and Riemann–Roch interfaces. The differential-dimension and independent-evaluation lemmas retain full AC, compact connected X and topological genus. Jacobi inversion applies the signed-divisor formula at degree g to obtain ℓ(D′)≥1, then uses an effective divisor of degree g. Principal-divisor degree zero, canonical-bundle sections, and both directions of the divisor/bundle equivalence are used faithfully. This is citation-interface review, not certification of every transitive supplier proof.
